title: The first queen: look for its check, not only the count
outcomes: In a race where both pawns will queen, looks for a check or capture by the first queen instead of only counting moves
Predicts how moving the black king off the queening file changes the result
Recognises a position that is not a race because a king stops the pawn

steps.text: Both sides will queen, and you have counted who is first (see the lesson *Pawn races: the square, and who queens first*). **Counting is only half.** Ask next what your first queen can do at once: capture the other pawn, cover its queening square, or check along the line where the second queen will appear. A check that also hits the new queen can win it.

steps.caption: White to move. Each pawn is one move from queening. The tablebase says White wins; one line is shown.

line.say: The queen checks along the h-file, where Black's new queen stands.
The white queen takes the black queen.

claims.statement: With White to move, White wins.
The queen on h8 attacks the king on h5.
Black's new queen stands on h1.

steps.text: **When it works.** Both pawns are free to queen, no king can interfere, and the first queen has a check or a capture on its first move. **When it fails.** The check disappears if the black king is not on that line, as in the next pair. Rule of thumb: before you count the moves, look for the first queen's check along the line to the second queen.

steps.title: Where are the kings?
steps.prompt: Each pawn is one move from queening and White queens first. In the second position only the black king has moved; in the third only the white king has. Predict each result, then check.
Before you answered, did you look for a check or a capture by the first queen, or did you only count moves? Which one did you do in the position where you were wrong?
